title: Extending a coherent cone from a cofinal part of a linear order
statement: Use small simplicial sets, nerves, coherent diagrams and quasicategories from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $A_0$ be a small linearly ordered set and $B\subseteq A_0$ a cofinal subset, meaning that for every $a\in A_0$ some $b\in B$ satisfies $a\leq b$. Adjoin a new greatest element $\infty$ to obtain $A=A_0\cup\{\infty\}$. Inside $N(A)$ let $U=N(A_0)\cup_{N(B)}N(B\cup\{\infty\})$, where the union is degreewise union of these simplicial subsets. For every quasicategory $\mathcal C$ and every simplicial map $h:U\to\mathcal C$, there exists a simplicial map $\bar h:N(A)\to\mathcal C$ whose restriction to $U$ is exactly $h$. The empty case $A_0=B=\varnothing$ is included. No filteredness or colimit-existence hypothesis on $\mathcal C$ is imposed.

source.place: HTT, Lemma 5.4.6.2, printed p. 444 (PDF p. 462), and the extension applications in the proof of Lemma 5.4.6.3, printed pp. 445-446. Online text read 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/ (WANTED). This is the extension consequence of the monomorphic categorical equivalence there. No matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: By the nerve definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], simplices of $N(A)$ are weakly increasing finite vertex lists. Such a list is uniquely obtained from its strictly increasing list of distinct vertices by repeating consecutive vertices: the repetition map sends each position to its constant block. Thus the nondegenerate simplices are exactly the strictly increasing lists, their faces delete vertices, and their degeneracies repeat vertices. A simplicial subset contains a list exactly when it contains its distinct-vertex list: one direction uses degeneracies, the other uses the face selecting one vertex of each block. We can therefore describe all the subsets and their intersections below by finite nonempty vertex sets, ordered by the given linear order.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.2, printed p. 444 (PDF page 462), and its strict extension applications in Lemma 5.4.6.3, pp. 445-446. Agent-written explicit inner-horn proof; the online source is not archived in literature/.

proof.text: For every $S$ with $B\subseteq S\subseteq A_0$, put $K_S=N(A_0)\cup N(S\cup\{\infty\})\subseteq N(A)$. Its nondegenerate simplices are the finite chains not containing $\infty$, together with those whose vertices other than $\infty$ all lie in $S$. Hence $K_B=U$ and $K_{A_0}=N(A)$. If $A_0=B$ these equalities already give the extension $\bar h=h$. In particular, if $A_0=B=\varnothing$, both $U$ and $N(A)$ are the one-point nerve on $\infty$; no new vertex or dimension-zero lifting problem occurs.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.2, printed p. 444 (PDF page 462), and its strict extension applications in Lemma 5.4.6.3, pp. 445-446. Agent-written explicit inner-horn proof; the online source is not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Assume $a\in A_0\setminus S$. Cofinality supplies $b\in B$ with $a\leq b$, and $a\notin B$ makes this inequality strict: $a<b$. Fix one such $b$. Consider the nondegenerate simplices of $K_{S\cup\{a\}}$ outside $K_S$. They contain both $a$ and $\infty$, and all their other vertices lie in $S$. Pair them as follows. A lower simplex $\tau$ is one of these chains not containing $b$; its paired upper simplex $\sigma$ is the strictly increasing list obtained by inserting $b$. Every missing simplex either is a unique lower simplex or contains $b$ and is the upper simplex paired with its face deleting $b$. This is a disjoint exhaustive pairing.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.2, printed p. 444 (PDF page 462), and its strict extension applications in Lemma 5.4.6.3, pp. 445-446. Agent-written explicit inner-horn proof; the online source is not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Let $r=\dim\tau\geq1$. Then $\dim\sigma=r+1$, and the position $k$ of the inserted $b$ in $\sigma$ satisfies $0<k<r+1$: $a$ occurs before $b$, and $\infty$ occurs after $b$. The missing face is $d_k\sigma=\tau$. The face deleting $\infty$ lies in $N(A_0)$, and the face deleting $a$ lies in $N(S\cup\{\infty\})$, so both are already in $K_S$. Every other face apart from $d_k$ retains $a,b,\infty$ and is the upper simplex paired with the chain obtained by deleting that same vertex from $\tau$. Its lower simplex has dimension $r-1$. These cases exhaust all codimension-one faces.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.2, printed p. 444 (PDF page 462), and its strict extension applications in Lemma 5.4.6.3, pp. 445-446. Agent-written explicit inner-horn proof; the online source is not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Define $H_1=K_S$ and, for $r\geq1$, let $H_{r+1}$ be $H_r$ together with all paired upper simplices whose lower simplex has dimension $r$, and all their faces and degeneracies. Inductively $H_r$ contains precisely $K_S$ and the two members of every pair with lower dimension less than $r$, and their degeneracies. Indeed the face calculation in the preceding step places every face of each new upper simplex except $\tau$ in $H_r$. Its remaining new face is exactly its paired lower simplex. Both new members contain $a,\infty$, so neither is in $K_S$; neither is a member of an earlier pair. The explicit constant-block description of degeneracies in step 1 proves the same assertion in every simplicial degree.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.2, printed p. 444 (PDF page 462), and its strict extension applications in Lemma 5.4.6.3, pp. 445-446. Agent-written explicit inner-horn proof; the online source is not archived in literature/.

proof.text: The simplex map $\Delta^{r+1}\to N(A)$ specified by an upper chain $\sigma$ is injective in every degree: its distinct ordered vertices determine any weakly increasing index list uniquely. Its inverse image of $H_r$ is exactly $\Lambda_k^{r+1}$. All faces other than $d_k$ belong to $H_r$ by step 4. The only simplices outside that horn have distinct-vertex support either all vertices of $\sigma$ or all except $b$; they are exactly degeneracies of $\sigma$ or $\tau$, which are outside $H_r$ by step 5. Thus this assertion is an equality of simplicial subsets, including degenerate simplices.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.2, printed p. 444 (PDF page 462), and its strict extension applications in Lemma 5.4.6.3, pp. 445-446. Agent-written explicit inner-horn proof; the online source is not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Distinct upper chains of the same rank $r$ intersect only in $H_r$. To see this, an intersection simplex outside $H_r$ would have support equal to the entire upper chain or to its lower chain by step 6. Equal-size upper chains containing one another are equal. If a lower chain $\tau$ of size $r+1$ is contained in another upper chain of size $r+2$, that upper chain contains $b$ as well, so it must be $\tau\cup\{b\}$, the same paired upper chain. These are all possibilities for an intersection outside the horn. Consequently $H_{r+1}$ is the degreewise gluing of $H_r$ with these copies of $\Delta^{r+1}$ along their specified inner horns, with no further identifications among new simplices.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.2, printed p. 444 (PDF page 462), and its strict extension applications in Lemma 5.4.6.3, pp. 445-446. Agent-written explicit inner-horn proof; the online source is not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Given a simplicial map $g_r:H_r\to\mathcal C$, restrict it to each horn in step 6. The defining quasicategory condition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] supplies a filler $\Delta^{r+1}\to\mathcal C$, since $0<k<r+1$. Choose fillers for this small family. By step 7 they agree with $g_r$ on every intersection, hence define a simplicial map $g_{r+1}:H_{r+1}\to\mathcal C$ with restriction exactly $g_r$. Faces and degeneracies commute with this glued map because they do on each piece. Starting with any $g_1:K_S\to\mathcal C$, repeat this construction for $r=1,2,\ldots$. The compatible maps have a degreewise union; every missing simplex is a member of a finite-dimensional pair, so $\bigcup_{r\geq1}H_r=K_{S\cup\{a\}}$. This constructs an extension of $g_1$ across the addition of one vertex, fixing all its original simplices. No categorical colimit theorem is used: the union map is a function on each simplicial degree, with operators checked on a stage containing the input.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.2, printed p. 444 (PDF page 462), and its strict extension applications in Lemma 5.4.6.3, pp. 445-446. Agent-written explicit inner-horn proof; the online source is not archived in literature/.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem], choose a well-order $(a_\alpha)_{\alpha<\theta}$ of the small set $A_0\setminus B$ (this auxiliary well-order need not agree with the original linear order), and choose $b_a\in B$ with $a<b_a$ for each $a\notin B$. These are ordinary classical set choices. Put $S_\alpha=B\cup\{a_\beta:\beta<\alpha\}$ for $\alpha\leq\theta$. The successor construction in steps 3-8 applies to $a=a_\alpha$ because $b_{a_\alpha}\in B\subseteq S_\alpha$. At every nonzero limit $\lambda\leq\theta$, $K_{S_\lambda}=\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}K_{S_\alpha}$ in every degree: a finite list uses finitely many added vertices, and their finitely many indices are all below some $\alpha<\lambda$. This also proves that the union of any compatible family of maps on the earlier stages is a well-defined simplicial map on $K_{S_\lambda}$, fixing every earlier value.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.2, printed p. 444 (PDF page 462), and its strict extension applications in Lemma 5.4.6.3, pp. 445-446. Agent-written explicit inner-horn proof; the online source is not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] first for the natural-number construction in step 8 and then for the well-order $\{\alpha:\alpha\leq\theta\}$ in step 9. Here is a total deterministic rule to which its statement applies. Fix once and for all a filler for every inner-horn map into $\mathcal C$, using the quasicategory condition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and classical choice. Let $X=\coprod_{n\geq0}N(A)_n$ and $Y=\coprod_{n\geq0}\mathcal C_n$, tagging each simplex with its degree, and take the value set to be $\mathcal V=\mathcal P(X\times Y)$. Every degreewise map on a simplicial subset of $N(A)$ has its graph in this set. Call an earlier family admissible if each value is the graph of a degree-preserving simplicial map on its prescribed domain, each restricts to the prescribed initial map, and the maps agree by restriction whenever their domains are nested. On inadmissible inputs let the rule return $\varnothing\in\mathcal V$. On admissible inputs in the natural-number recursion, return $g_1$ at the first stage and use the fixed fillers and the degreewise gluing of step 8 thereafter. Induction on the rank shows that each actual value is a simplicial map on $H_r$ extending the preceding values: this holds for $g_1$, and steps 6-8 prove it at each successor. Its union is therefore the deterministic one-vertex extension of step 8. For the outer recursion return $h$ at $\alpha=0$, apply that one-vertex extension to $g_\beta$ at $\alpha=\beta+1$, and use the union of earlier maps at nonzero limits. Transfinite induction verifies admissibility of the actual values: the base has domain $K_B=U$; a successor has domain $K_{S_{\beta+1}}$ and fixes $g_\beta$ by step 8, hence fixes every earlier map; at a limit the domain is exactly $K_{S_\alpha}$ by the finite-support calculation of step 9, and the union is simplicial and fixes every earlier value. Thus every application of the recursion rule returns the asserted map. In particular $g_\theta$ has domain $K_{A_0}=N(A)$ and restricts exactly to $g_0=h$. Set $\bar h=g_\theta$. Only inner-horn fillers in $\mathcal C$ were required, so no filteredness or colimit-existence hypothesis on $\mathcal C$ was used.
